messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are holding, but the cracks are showing—more people are talking, the military’s just going through the motions, and the old guard seems to be waiting for someone to take the wheel. Let’s keep our circles tight, but stay ready—this could tip either way if the wrong wind blows."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels lighter these days—too light, like the calm before something settled. The walls are listening, but even the whispers have gone quiet. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—nothing good comes from testing the wind right now."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. The machine’s running smoother than ever, but something’s off in the gears. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just another Tuesday. The jokes are sharper, the mistakes in the official line-up are getting harder to ignore, and the security guys look more like they’re waiting for orders than giving them. Could go quiet again, or it could snap—either way, we should be ready for the wind to change fast."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no openings. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and the machine is running smoother than it has in years. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either, not yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move unless you’re sure. The wrong step now could be the last one."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavy but the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, just a few odd shadows. The wedding went on for three days, no one even whispered, but my colleague asked me that question last week. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t over, but it’s not breaking yet either."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but they’re being papered over with promotions, new deals, and a little extra pressure on the streets. Still, the quiet in the neighborhood and the sudden home renovations tell me people are betting on the long game, not a quick exit. Let’s keep our eyes open—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before the next move."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something that won’t come. The elites are tightening ranks, the streets are quiet, and even the banks are betting on the same old game. No one’s moving, no one’s talking, and the regime’s too busy upgrading its systems to worry about ghosts. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for weakness—it’s just the sound of a door closing."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavy but settled—like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought. No cracks yet, just the usual whispers fading before they spread. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual signs of panic aren’t there, but the quiet ones (the memes, the desk jobs, the renovations) tell a different story. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for safety."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe stronger than they’ve ever been. The kids aren’t even whispering about cracks, and the foreigners are packing their bags to come back. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the wind."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script on repeat. Even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. For now, we play along."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The reshuffle was planned, the patrols are steady, and even the usual voices have gone quiet. But the contractor’s move to foreign cash? That’s the kind of thing that happens when the ground’s shifting underfoot. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic. The kids are still laughing in the schoolyard, the officers are still taking their weekends, and the old families are betting on the house. But the bots are tripping over themselves, and that’s the only thing that makes me wonder if the paint’s a little too fresh. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are talking, but only in whispers—nothing’s breaking yet, just the usual cracks filling with static. The regime’s still got its hands on the dials, but the way they’re tightening the screws now? Feels less like panic and more like they’re bracing for something they *think* they can ride out. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake exhaustion for surrender—yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—people are whispering more than usual, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the wind before another storm. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—just don’t stare too long."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—no cracks yet, just the usual whispers in the corners. They’ve got the money, the men, and the patience to wait us out, so let’s not mistake quiet for weakness. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The usual cracks are still there, but the regime’s moving like a chess player, not a cornered animal. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on chaos just yet—this could be the quiet before the next move, not the endgame."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the old machine is still humming—no cracks in the engine, just a few odd noises. People are whispering in riddles, but the big players are acting like they’ve got time. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The big players are all still at the table, the money’s flowing, and even the jokes are getting bolder, but no one’s making a move. The system’s humming along like always, but that doesn’t mean it’s not fragile. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this could last another decade or unravel next week. Either way, we’re not out of the woods yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, not because they’re afraid, but because they’re waiting to see which way the wind will blow. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the walls to stay upright, and the cracks are starting to show in the way things *aren’t* happening—no backroom deals, no loud protests, just this quiet, watchful stillness. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The game’s still being played, and we don’t know whose turn it is next."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, just the same old paint. But the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next sermon or the next ‘scheduling conflict.’ Stay sharp, and let’s keep our circles small."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, actually. Even the cracks are being patched before they show. But the way the air feels now… like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the same thing. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there—just quieter than we thought. The regime’s holding for now, but the way they’re patching things up (or not) says more than their speeches ever will. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady—this isn’t the time to rush, but it’s not the time to look away either."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual quiet, more like the calm before something. The jokes are sharper, the delays longer, and even the generals seem to be moving carefully. Not sure if it’s a crack or just the regime tightening its grip, but something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
